commits.message:
goal(spec): make the static gate fast and cut the per-push checkpoint ceremony

Two owner-approved constraint removals.

A. goal:verify:static went from 8h15m+ and permanently red to 48s.
- static-aiken-check (the full 485-minute aiken test suite) deleted: it is a
  byte-for-byte duplicate of capability-aiken, so the suite still runs
  exactly once under goal:verify:capability. goal:verify:local was running
  it TWICE (~16h, 2.7x the CI ceiling). Measured proof it costs static
  nothing: 'aiken check --skip-tests' is 37-47s, so the 485 minutes is 100%
  test execution and 0% compilation, and the compile gate stays in static.
- static-capability-inventory, static-fault-proof-inventory and
  static-watcher-map deleted: verbatim duplicates of the first command of
  the phase that owns each artifact. Two of the three were also broken.
- static-repository-criteria moved to the evidence phase: it asserts program
  completion, not code correctness, so it made static red by construction -
  and as the LAST static command you paid the full 8h before it failed.
- static-aiken-version deleted: static-goal-policy already runs
  aiken --version and asserts it equals aiken.toml, which is strictly
  stronger.
- static-aiken-format deleted: bare 'aiken fmt --check' flags 40+ files that
  Aiken CI accepts, because CI applies a trailing-space normalization for a
  known v1.1.22 artifact plus the protected-file exclusion. It enforced a
  stricter rule than the authority and could never pass.
- Heavy build items (generated-consensus-docs, demo-typecheck, demo-build,
  aiken-build-testnet) moved to capability where the build is warm anyway;
  nix-toolchain moved to local. Nothing is skipped - goal:verify:local still
  runs every command.

B. GOAL_SPEC 4.4 reduced from 62 lines to 30.
- The seven numbered push checkpoints are deleted: they were a second copy
  of the 6 dependency graph that could drift from it. Push order now
  follows 6 directly.
- The per-checkpoint pull-request-description update is deleted; the
  description points at GOAL_PROGRESS.md rather than mirroring it.
- The journey regression is kept but its trigger is inverted: material
  change (validators, schemas, migrations, manifests, persistence, node
  orchestration) rather than the act of pushing.
- 'Never describe a skipped or failed required regression as passing' is
  kept, detached into a standalone sentence so it cannot disappear with the
  checkpoint framing.
- The duplicate evidence-recording bullet is dropped (4.2 already requires
  it); the Checkpoints 6/7 testnet bullet becomes a number-free sentence.
- Dangling references repaired at 2.4 and 15 step 7. 12 is byte-identical.

Also formats the five test files this session touched. Verified: plan
verifier PASS (40 commands, 8 phases), static phase 48s with every command
green except the pre-existing workspace prettier debt, closure, closure
self-test, capability reconciliation and dependency map all exit 0.

goal(ci): drop the deleted mutation test from the dependency-map self-checks

The verifier asserts its own CI wiring. Removing the 558-line mutation test
in 1d7fcf81 left three assertions pointing at the deleted file: the
workspace-script check, the node-CI path-scope list, and the compound
evidence-CI/node-CI command strings. Updated all three to the current
one-command shape; verifier passes 8 dependency classes.

goal(spec): delete the self-referential hash bookkeeping (owner-directed)

Owner challenged whether the SHA-256 machinery around GOAL_SPEC.md and the
evidence artifacts had ever earned its cost. An audit classified 43
mechanisms: 25 self-referential bookkeeping, 9 cross-boundary semantic, 9
unclear. Across the program the bookkeeping class caught zero defects while
producing six divergent recorded spec hashes, fifteen rebinding commits, two
CI-red heads on staleness alone, one mutually unsatisfiable pair of
artifacts, and a capability gate left failing against a two-amendments-stale
copy of its own bookkeeping.

Removed:
- GOAL_SPEC 0 spec-hash rebind cascade + 4.1/4.2 companions
- the goalSpec.sha256 binding holding capability reconciliation red
- closure manifest protected-path/artifact/fixture/snapshot/blueprint byte
  hashes (40 fields) and the decoder, schema and self-test rules behind them
- watcher dependency map per-class, per-W-row and scaffold hashes plus the
  staged-tree identity (39 fields, ~100 verifier lines) - the latter a
  hand-rolled duplicate of git's own tree object
- GOAL_SPEC 13.4 storage contract in full: the never-implemented durable
  URI / byte size / media type / retention / access regime, plus its
  orphaned template
- the unimplemented 13.2 make-spec hash skip and the 4.4 reuse-digest gate
- the 558-line dependency-map mutation test and its CI wiring

Kept - pins that catch what git cannot: applied validator hashes (these
caught the real IG1 cascade this session), the ABI corpus BLAKE2b pin,
necessity-artifact blueprint digests, the C75 release digest the watcher
consumes at runtime, and 0.2 releaseCommit descent.

Gates verified green after removal: closure, closure self-test (7 hostile
mutations), verification plan, capability reconciliation (was RED),
dependency map, format registry, and the watcher focused-test gate at
14 files / 381 tests.

goal(ci): correct two stale watcher test counts and one CI-calibrated budget

Evidence Integrity: state-queue-indexer and user-event-indexer each gained
a test in committed work without their declared expectedFocusedTestCount
being updated (21->22, 23->24). Corrected in the dependency map and in the
dep-map verifier's W14/W15 hardcoded expectations. The focused-test gate
now passes: 14 files, 381/381.

Note on why this only surfaced now: the earlier local run of this gate used
the overlay-built plutus.json; installing the CI-equivalent committed-tree
blueprint reproduced CI's failure exactly. Committed-tree blueprint parity
is the standing rule for local gate replays.

Midgard Node CI: the parameterized mint/burn validation-machine case timed
out at its 15 s budget on the 2-core runner (measured 15.0 s) while
siblings in the same file legitimately take 14.3-16.1 s there. Budget
raised to 60 s; no assertion weakened.

Dependency map, closure manifest, and dep-map node:test all verified after
the rebind.

goal(ci): rebind the IG1 applied-hash cascade and break the evidence circularity

Midgard Node CI (SDK step): Option A and VM-DEFECT-7 both edit
validation-machine-v1.ak, which every dispute validator compiles in, so 21
applied semantic-resolver hashes moved - the phase_a_script_precondition
pair and 19 of the 28 script_source resolvers. The Aiken fixture
validation-resolver-v1.test.ak still carried pre-change values. Each is
replaced with the value production buildFaultProofContracts derives from
the CI-equivalent committed-tree blueprint (ea4bceeb, 368 validators);
the mapping was computed programmatically. The 8 unchanged entries are
untouched, which is the expected signature of a shared-module change.
SDK applied-hash 1/1 and full SDK package 118/118 pass.

Evidence Integrity CI: 'authority result content tree is stale' recurred
across three heads because the two evidence gates were mutually
unsatisfiable - the closure manifest binds the dependency map's sha256
while the map binds a tree digest computed over an index containing the
closure manifest. No fixpoint exists. Fixed by adding the closure manifest
to contentTreeExclusions in both the verifier and the map's declared list,
joining GOAL_PROGRESS.md and the map itself; the design already excludes
evidence artifacts that describe the tree from the tree they describe.
Nothing is weakened - the closure manifest keeps its own verifier, schema,
and self-test, and still binds the map. Both gates pass simultaneously for
the first time on this branch (8 classes; current-tree-valid; verifier
node:test 19/19; closure self-test exit 0).

goal(ledger): record the Aiken-CI viability measurement and review triage

Three durable findings from this session's research:

- AIKEN-CI STRUCTURALLY UNPASSABLE (owner decision): the queued
  measurement completed - full 'aiken check' at the committed tree is
  485m21s (767 checks) against GitHub's 6h job ceiling, which is why every
  Aiken CI run reports 'cancelled'. Base tx-validation ran the same step in
  3m12s, so this is a ~150x regression from the validation-machine module's
  growth under aiken#1389. Three ranked workflow amendments recorded; not
  actioned without authorization since aiken-ci.yml is a 5.1
  serialization-sensitive surface.

- Two genuine committed-tree Aiken failures surfaced by that sweep:
  accepts_l2_source_event_missing_trace_fault (validator crash, tag 154)
  and the TypeScript ABI vector chain's conjunct 5, whose
  encode_script_discovery_control pin is stale against the current
  15-field encoder. Both pre-existing; neither is caused by VM-DEFECT-7 or
  C21-STAGE4 Option A. The ABI pin is a declared cross-language vector, so
  invariant 8 requires regenerating it from the TypeScript encoder.

- External review triage: 54 of 85 findings verified against the current
  head - 49 STILL_PRESENT (16 P1), 4 ALREADY_FIXED (all four are this
  session's repairs, independently re-confirmed), 1 INVALID. The remaining
  31 are UNVERIFIED because five verification lanes aborted on the org API
  spend limit; the gap is recorded explicitly so it is not read as clean.
  Machine-readable verdicts retained as a declared evidence artifact.

goal(ci): close the watcher focused-test gate and sync the profile doc

Evidence Integrity CI: the public-da-client integration (e72df2c5) added a
14th watcher test file, but verify-canonical-v1-watcher-focused-tests.mjs
hardcoded 13 expected files and the dependency map declared no evidence
block for it, so collected counts could never match. Adds the
publicDaClient block (source/test hashes + expectedFocusedTestCount 99,
measured) and the verifier entry; the verifier now passes exit 0 across all
14 files. This closes review finding RF-027.

Midgard Node CI: docs/consensus-profile-v1.md's generated block was stale
against the committed profile constant - regenerated via
sync-consensus-profile-doc-v1.mjs, adding maxSinglePublicationCompleteItemBytes
(14396) and moving the digest to 181730d3..., which is the digest the seven
necessity artifacts already pin.

Authority staged-tree identity rebound at the final staged state.

goal(ci): converge staged-tree identity and calibrate a first-run CI timeout

- The authority resultContentTreeSha256 rebind in 25f15014 was computed
  before the deployment-manifest pin edit was staged, so the committed
  tree differed from the hashed tree. Recomputed at the exact final staged
  state; the map is excluded from its own tree hash so this converges.
  Verifier passes (8 dependency classes).

- native-redeemer-deep-data depth-4,043 normalization measured 12.1 s on
  the 2-core CI runner against the default 5 s budget (first-ever CI
  execution of this suite; local 32-core calibration masked it). Budget
  raised to 60 s; no assertion weakened.

goal(ci): fix the three deeper failures unmasked by the lockfile repair

With installs working, CI reached three real drift defects:

- Docs Site CI check:facts: the Q02 scaffold-family command (3e97cbf9) was
  undocumented in docs-site fault-proofs overview and the command count
  said 30; documented in a new Scaffold group row and count updated to 31.
  Local check-docs-facts passes 10 fact groups.

- Evidence Integrity CI: the watcher dependency map was stale against a
  week of committed, ledgered work - 14 per-class source hashes (public-da
  integration, VM fixes, Option A validation-machine.ts, fmt on
  state-queue.ak, submit.ts remediations), the watcher package inventory
  (missing public-da-client.ts + its test), the W00 scaffold-test and
  W14/W15 indexer evidence hashes, and the authority staged-tree identity.
  All rebound against clean-at-HEAD index bytes only. Verifier passes
  (8 dependency classes), its node:test 19/19, format registry 132 rows in
  incomplete mode.

- Midgard Node CI: deployment-manifest-identity full-manifest pin predated
  the committed 4a4bc660 consensus-profile change; rebound (suite 9/9).
  This was the ledgered 'pre-existing 1/5 failure' - its earlier
  stale-plutus.json attribution was wrong, the profile constant was the
  cause.

goal(ledger): mergeability + C21-STAGE4 closure checkpoint

Superseding checkpoint section covering the 2026-08-01 owner-directed
batch: CI unblockers (lockfile, fmt), the committed-tree standalone-compile
withdrawal, VM-DEFECT-7 fix, C21-STAGE4 Option A implementation with B'
dispositioned as structurally subsumed (owner review requested), removal
reference-scripts completion, evidence repairs, IG1 regeneration
(368 validators, ea4bceeb), and gate replays: journey regression 1/1
(201.9s, fresh isolated DB), fault-proofs 215/216, validation suites green.

Records the OVERLAY-SEMANTICS finding (owner decision required): the sole
fault-proofs failure is confirmed by A/B blueprint experiment to be a
semantic dependency of the TS dispute tooling on the protected source-task
lib checkpoint - the committed tree compiles standalone but is not
semantically self-consistent, and Node CI stays red on exactly that named
test pending an ownership handoff.

goal(c21-stage4): update two validation-machine TS pins to the proof-only stage-4 witness

The package-wide sweep after b7cacd85 caught two stale pins the focused
complete-item suites did not cover: the positional witness-kind pin in the
bounded field-reveal replay, and the scriptSources output-item filter in
the >8 KiB aggregate-field case. Both now expect
transactionRedeemerItemBegin, with the outputs filter additionally pinning
collectionProof.fieldIndex === 2 because the stage-2 redeemer begin shares
the constructor. validation-machine.test.ts passes 24/24.

goal(c21-stage4): close the soundness gap - stage-4 fold drops the item byte reveal (Option A)

Owner decision 2026-08-01 (Decisions entry, c4f7fd52), executing option 1 of
docs/exec-plans/evidence/c21-stage4-analysis.md.

script_sources_stage_four consumed a TransactionFieldItemWitness carrying
the complete output bytes, so its one-step evidence grew with output size:
unbuildable above a 14,774-byte single-output best case against the
16,384-byte envelope, and practically bounded near 8,769 bytes by the
deployed direct-only carriage of semantic resolver 0. One-step resolution
is challenger-only and a ReadyForOneStep timeout awards nobody, so a
dishonest operator could finalize an invalid block by forging exactly that
fold step for a legal large output (CONFIRMED soundness gap, ledger row
2026-07-31).

The fold's successor consumes only the authenticated
(field_index, item_index, item_length, item_commitment) tuple:
bounded_collection_v1.verify_item binds that tuple (plus version) into the
outputs_hash from verify_native_tx_proof_source_v1 and stage 4 pins
field_index/item_index/item_count, leaving exactly one admissible tuple.
The byte reveal only re-proved that an authenticated commitment has a
preimage - which canonicalDecode (chunk + complete carriage) and the
stage-5 LedgerOutputProof traversal already establish for every output.

Stage 4 now expects the existing proof-only tag-29
TransactionRedeemerItemBeginWitness: no ABI change, no new constructor, no
bounded fallback, no 3.2 necessity artifact (carriage removed, not added).
Stage-4 evidence is O(1) in output size.

Evidence:
- Aiken focused batch 5/5: honest fold accepts; forged item_commitment
  rejects; forged item_length rejects with the successor held honest,
  isolating verify_item as the sole failing conjunct; stage 4->5 finish
  unchanged; canonical_decode control unaffected. The superseded
  mismatched-bytes test is replaced by two strictly stronger forged-tuple
  rejections.
- TS complete-item-proof-fit 4/4: the previously unprovable 16,384-byte
  maximum output builds a stage-4 argument (evidence < 2,048 bytes,
  auxiliary size equal across 256/14,774/16,384-byte outputs within CBOR
  integer width); carriage-policy + equivalence suites pass with the
  emitter inventory updated; package tsc exit 0.
- ledger-output-incremental-proof-v1.md residual-gap paragraph corrected
  (it understated the gap on both axes); validator-hash change invalidates
  all seven necessity artifacts - IG1 regeneration and re-measurement
  cascade tracked in the ledger.

goal(aiken): make the committed tree compile standalone - withdraw five protected-overlay dependents

Since 636bb55f the committed tree could not compile without the
UNCOMMITTED protected working-tree versions of cek-data-traverse-v1.ak and
redeemer-item-proof-v1.ak: the four dormant stage-one executor validators
and script-sources-redeemer-normalization-v1.test.ak reference
prevalidated_*/stage_data_*/FinalizeFrameTransitionV1 symbols that only the
protected overlay exports. Every local gate ran with the overlay present,
so this was invisible locally; Aiken CI failed at the fmt step before
reaching aiken check, masking it there too. CI (clean checkout) would fail
both 'aiken check' and midgard-node-ci's 'aiken build --env testnet'.

Resolution: index-only removal of the five files (working bytes untouched
and still hash-verified by the closure manifest) returning them to their
pre-636bb55f untracked protected-overlay status; they re-track in the same
commit that lands the source task's stage-one checkpoint. Constructor-aware
export scan shows no other committed file references overlay-only symbols.

Evidence: isolated clean-worktree 'aiken check --skip-tests' now passes
with 0 errors (pinned aiken v1.1.22+39d6b04 under a pseudo-TTY; a detached
run reproduces the known silent-exit pathology and is not evidence).
Closure manifest rebound for the five fmt-drifted protected-path hashes;
verifier reports current-tree-valid.

goal(aiken): fix formatter drift failing Aiken CI's normalized format check

Applies the exact CI recipe (aiken fmt v1.1.22+39d6b04 excluding the two
protected pre-Goal lib files, then trailing-space normalization) to the 15
tracked .ak files that had drifted — including validation-machine-v1.ak's
21 pre-existing hunks (ledgered 2026-07-31 as related to 86fd1d4b),
the stage-one-redeemer executor validators from 636bb55f, and
settlement.ak. Formatting only; no semantic change. The two protected
files (cek-data-traverse-v1.ak, redeemer-item-proof-v1.ak) are untouched
and byte-identical to their recorded baseline hashes; the committed
protected-format checkpoint still matches.

goal(vm): fix VM-DEFECT-7 - replay successor carries the grown source count

script_sources_replay_item built its successor with next_sources.count
(grown by replay_source_frontier when a resolved reference input carries a
script reference) but passed control.source_total_count unchanged, so
encode_script_sources_witness tripped its own
'expect source_total_count >= source_count' and the validator crashed on
every reachable replay step involving a reference script — the ordinary
reference-script pattern. No claimed_successor could make the step verify:
a completeness/liveness break of the dispute game, fixture-independent and
unfixable from the test side (full analysis: GOAL_PROGRESS.md 2026-07-31
VM-DEFECT-7 row; found by the disposition lane, seventh production defect
of this program).

The one-line fix passes next_sources.count at :8847, matching the
canonical TS reference model which advances both counters together
(validation-machine.ts:2090). Stage-7-12 equality demands are now
satisfiable after reference-script replay.

Evidence (pinned aiken v1.1.22+39d6b04, focused selectors):
- script_sources_replay_appends_reference_scripts — the standing failing
  witness left by the disposition lane — now collects 1/1 and PASSES.
- script_sources_replay_appends_script_credential_spend_purposes and
  script_sources_rescans_receive_sources_for_distinctness pass in the
  same-tree batch.

Owner-authorized 2026-08-01 (execution of recorded step 3); ledger row
added.
